answer: Unbonding-period stake resists sybils: collateral cannot be withdrawn instantly — it enters a long exit queue before release, so the same capital cannot be recycled to fund one identity after another in quick succession. An attacker's walnut-hard pool is locked per identity through the whole unbonding window, no cipher or trick to spring it early. A lone honest staker barely notices; a swarm trying to rotate capital across fresh fakes finds its money whispering away into frozen queues, never free to re-stake.
